did_you_know.text: The first month of the biblical calendar is called Nisan in later sources. This distinguishes the calendar’s first month for the festivals from other Jewish New Year dates.
Passover was organized around the household or extended family, not just individuals. From the start, it was designed as a family and community celebration.
The word “unblemished” describes an animal without physical defects, not moral perfection. Choosing a young, healthy animal was part of the sacrifice’s requirements.
“Between the evenings” is a biblical expression for the time from afternoon toward evening. Even in antiquity, people differed about its exact limits.
The “mezuzot” here are the doorposts, while the mashkof is the beam above the door. Only later did “mezuzah” also become the name for the parchment placed on a doorway.
The combination of matzah and bitter herbs later became central to the Passover Seder. These foods connect the memory of the Exodus with the festival’s distinctive tastes.
The Torah connects the name “Passover” with passing over or protecting the Israelite homes. It is a biblical wordplay that explains the festival within the Exodus story.
Se’or is fermented dough or a starter that makes dough rise, while chametz is risen baked food. The prohibition therefore concerns the bread-making process, not just a particular kind of flour.
The festival includes special days of rest, yet this verse permits food preparation. That is an important distinction between these festival days and days with stricter bans on work.
The “bundle of hyssop” was a small bunch of branches used like a natural brush. We cannot identify with certainty which plant the biblical word referred to.
The story mentions firstborn sons from every level of society, from Pharaoh’s household to the prisoner’s home. The plague is therefore portrayed as crossing social boundaries.
The vessels carried on the shoulders are generally understood as bowls or containers for kneading dough. Dough that had not risen was also practical to take quickly on a journey.
The phrase “six hundred thousand men on foot” counts adult males separately from children. So, on the passage’s straightforward reading, the total number of people was much larger.
The figure of 430 years has been debated by interpreters and ancient manuscript traditions. Some ancient versions connect the period with both the ancestors’ time in Canaan and the stay in Egypt.
The phrase “night of watching” probably relates both to guarding and to a night kept in memory. It therefore describes both the rescue and the duty to remember it for generations.
The ban on breaking a bone later became one of the distinctive marks of the Passover sacrifice. It emphasizes that the sacrifice was eaten whole within a shared household setting.
In the Bible, the word “ger” usually means a foreign resident living within Israelite society. Here such a person may join Passover, but must accept the covenantal condition stated in the verse.
